newsitem.title: UK: UK forces to get 500 mln stg identification system.
newsitem.headline: UK forces to get 500 mln stg identification system.

text.p: The British Government said on Tuesday it planned to invite competitive tenders by July for the first phase of a 500 million pound electronic identification system to enable the country's armed forces to distinguish friend from foe.
Junior defence minister John Spellar said the sophisticated question-and-answer system would provide substantial work for British industry.
The system, known as Successor Identification Friend or Foe (SIFF), would be fitted on a wide range of ships and aircraft and on certain air defence installations.
It would be compatible with equipment used by Britain's NATO allies, Spellar said in a written parliamentary answer.
He said SIFF would protect British forces from inadvertent attack by their own side and would improve their prospects of avoiding detection by hostile units.

The competition will be for an initial integration study and planning phase, following which a prime contractor would be selected, who would be responsible for the supply and implementation of SIFF equipment, Spellar said.
